title: 1968 AHSME Problem 18
statement: Side \(AB\) of triangle \(ABC\) has length \(8\) inches. Line \(DEF\) is drawn parallel to \(AB\) so that \(D\) is on segment \(AC,\) and \(E\) is on segment \(BC.\) Line \(AE\) extended bisects angle \(FEC.\) If \(DE\) has length \(5\) inches, then the length of \(CE,\) in inches, is:

solutions.text:
Put \(G\) on the extension of \(AE\) beyond \(E.\) The bisector condition gives \(\angle FEG=\angle GEC.\) Since \(FE\parallel AB,\) we have \(\angle FEG=\angle BAE.\) Also, rays \(EG\) and \(EA\) are opposite, as are rays \(EC\) and \(EB,\) so \(\angle GEC=\angle AEB.\) Thus triangle \(ABE\) is isosceles and \(BE=AB=8.\) Similar triangles \(CDE\) and \(CAB\) give \(\frac{CE}{CE+8}=\frac58.\) Hence \(8CE=5CE+40,\) so \(CE=\frac{40}{3}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: Put \(G\) on the extension of \(AE\) beyond \(E\), so the bisector condition is \(\angle FEG=\angle GEC\)
After showing \(BE=AB,\) use similarity of \(CDE\) and \(CAB\)
